reports.title: Samiyo Farah
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: Observation protocol - there is no national guidance/policy on the observation of children and adolescents within specialist mental health units. At present, clinicians are forced to adopt/adapt policies applied to adults with mental health issues. The care needs of young people are quite different to those of adults.
concerns.hazard: lack of national observation guidance for children and adolescents in specialist mental health units

concerns.quote: Communication/contact between transferring establishments - there is no formal policy/protoco! in use/between the private sector and the NHS detailing steps that should be taken (and by whom) upon transfer of patients between sectors, thus risking that not all key information (both verbal and written) is properly communicated before, during and after transfer. concerns.hazard: absence of formal transfer protocol between private sector and NHS causing communication breakdown

concerns.quote: There appears to have been an inconsistency of approach following Miss [name redacted] admissions to A & E. She was referred directly to a Psychiatrist on the second attendance when she was clearly unwell but had not managed to self-harm but was not on the first attendance when she had taken an overdose. This also raises the question as to whether she ought to have been referred (to a Psychiatrist) on the 31° October 2012.
concerns.hazard: inconsistent referral of Miss Farah to psychiatry across A&E attendances

reports.title: Kimberley Lindfield
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: All patients presenting with symptoms of mental illness/mental disorder and/or after reported self harm/suicidal behaviour will now be automatically referred for a mental health assessment to be conducted as soon as possible whether that referral is from A&E or any ward. Pending that assessment mental health staff can give advice by phone concerning the patient's interim care and management.
promises.summary: Automatic referral for mental health assessment upon presentation of symptoms or self-harm, with phone advice pending assessment

links.explanation: Both reports highlight the absence of a clear, written policy governing how patient observations should be conducted and recorded. The earlier report focuses on child/adolescent observation in specialist units, while the later report concerns observation protocols linked to mental health assessments after self‑harm.
links.earlier_quote: Observation protocol - there is no national guidance/policy on the observation of children and adolescents within specialist mental health units. At present, clinicians are forced to adopt/adapt policies applied to adults with mental health issues.
links.later_quote: Whenever an increased level of observations is initiated pending a mental health assessment because of the concern about a patient's mental state and/or self harrm/suicidal behaviour there should be a clear written policy or protocol setting out what those observations actually involve (e.g. what 1 in every 15 minutes means and precisely what should be recorded)

links.explanation: Both reports highlight deficiencies in the observation documentation process for patients requiring heightened monitoring. The earlier report notes missing detail on who and when observations are recorded, while the later report calls for a clear written policy defining exactly what observations entail and how they should be recorded.
